mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the previous three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of quarters where FEDFUNDS rises by > 0.75% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 falls > 2% y/y.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods where UNRATE > 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% month-over-month, coinciding with rising raw material prices (RSAFS), signals input cost inflation and supply chain stress, which compresses profit margins and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1% m/m AND RSAFS rises > 2% m/m
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods meeting the dual INDPRO/RSAFS trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900K units for three consecutive months signals weakness in the residential construction sector, which negatively impacts materials and financial firms and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where HOUST < 900K for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% and a federal funds rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals a policy-induced disinflation regime, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS > 5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods meeting the CPIAUCSL/FEDFUNDS trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 300K in a single month signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where PAYEMS increases by > 300K in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An above-trend acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 up > 0.5% m/m after two consecutive months of flat or negative growth) signals a recovery in household demand, which lifts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 0.5% m/m after two months of <= 0% growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting the GDPC1 acceleration trigger.
